key_insight: Linking fracture-tip sampling distance to mesh resolution enables convergent stress intensity factor estimates where conventional nearest-tip sampling fails.
engineering_relevance: More reliable stress intensity factors support fracture-propagation decisions in computational solid mechanics.
method: Extract stress intensity factors using two-point displacement correlation.
Derive a sampling-distance scaling law by balancing asymptotic truncation and numerical discretization errors.
Validate with quadratic finite elements, quarter-point finite elements, and multi-point stress approximation finite volumes.
evidence_signal: On pure-mode and mixed-mode fracture benchmarks, scaling-based sampling produced decreasing errors under mesh refinement across all three methods, unlike nearest-tip sampling.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify the scaling formula or its parameters, so implementation requires consulting the full paper.
paper_title: A scaling law for numerical computation of fracture stress intensity factors
